title: HR Administrator
description:
Job Title: HR Administrator

Location: Sharston, Manchester M22 4 SN

Salary: £27,411.66 per annum

Job type: Full time, Permanent

About us:

Established in 2000, Express Solicitors is an award-winning, no win no fee law firm specialising exclusively in personal injury claims. Headquartered in Manchester, we support clients nationwide across all areas of personal injury, including employers' liability, serious injury, clinical negligence, occupiers' and public liability, road traffic accidents and industrial disease.

We are ranked 64th in The Lawyer UK Top 200, out of more than 10,000 law firms nationwide, and after achieving a 20% year-on-year growth, Express Solicitors are the largest personal injury claimant firm in the UK.

Our commitment to outstanding client care is reflected in our Trustpilot rating of 4.8 (Excellent), placing us among the highest-rated firms in the sector.

About The Role:

We are currently recruiting for a HR Administrator to provide administrative support to our HR Team. This is an exciting opportunity for a talented administrator to join our team and gain valuable HR specialist experience. The right candidate will have the chance to develop their HR career.

Responsibilities:
- Maintain accurate absence records by updating holiday, sickness, medical, and authorised leave information within the HR system.
- Verify that employees enter their data correctly on the HR platform.
- Send a daily absence summary email to all staff.
- Respond to routine staff enquiries in a timely and helpful manner.
- Support the HR team with various projects, such as absenteeism initiatives, company newsletters, HR system improvements, and updates to policies and procedures.
- Coordinate with new starters once an offer is made, including preparing and issuing employment contracts, requesting references, and organising their system setup.
- Deliver induction sessions for new starters.
- Complete checklists for new hires, internal promotions, and leavers to ensure smooth transitions. This includes collaborating with Department Heads and the IT team to share relevant information promptly.
- Ensure personnel files are kept accurate, up-to-date, and well organised.
- Provide general administrative support including filing, scanning, and taking minutes during employee meetings.
- Work with benefits providers, generate ad hoc reports, and liaise with Department Managers as needed.
- Carry out any additional ad hoc duties as required.

Person Specification:
- GCSE Maths and English at Grade 5 or above (or international equivalent).
- Strong administrative and organisational skills.
- Good numerical ability.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office, especially Excel, Word, Outlook, and PowerPoint.
- Flexible and able to prioritise tasks effectively in a dynamic environment.
- Resilient and capable of working under pressure.
- Willing and eager to learn.
- Excellent understanding of confidentiality, with the ability to handle sensitive information discreetly.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Confident and professional telephone manner.
- High level of accuracy and strong attention to detail.
- Demonstrated ability to coordinate and manage information effectively.
- Ability to thrive in a fast-paced work environment.
- Previous HR administration experience and an understanding of UK employment law are desirable but not essential.
- A relevant HR qualification is an advantage.

Salary & Hours:
- Salary of £27,411.66 based on 39.5 hours
- Our standard working hours are 8:30am to 5:30pm Monday-Thursday and 8:30am to 5pm Friday.

Benefits:
- Hybrid Working - 3/2 hybrid working pattern after probation.
- 23 Days Holiday - Rising to 26 days, plus bank/public holidays.
- Extra Holidays - 3 holiday buy backs and an extra day for your birthday after service length requirement.
- Looking After Your Health - Private medical insurance available after 2 years' service, annual flu jab and Employee Assistance Programme.
- Looking After Your Well-being - 24/7 onsite Gym, Netball/Football team, 10km Manchester team and more.
- Work Life / Balance - Active social committee with generous departmental and firm-wide social budget.

Recruitment Process:

Interviews will be conducted by MS Teams and will include scenario-based questioning.

Our employees are our most important asset, we rate skill and ability above all else and our recruitment policy encourages applications from all.

Please click APPLY to be redirected to our website to complete your application.

Candidates with the relevant experience or job titles of; HR Assistant, Human Resources Assistant, Human Resources Executive, HR Executive, Human Resources Administrator, HR Advisor, Human Resources Advisor, HR Generalist, Human Resources Admin, HR Officer, HR Admin may also be considered for this role.

£28,000 - £29,000 per annum + quarterly bonus
Manchester City Centre - predominantly office-based with flexible working available
Permanent

Sellick Partnership is working with a well-established SME consultancy based in Manchester city centre who are looking for an Accounts Assistant to join their growing finance team permanently. This is a business that has grown significantly and counts some of the UK's most recognisable names among its client base. They're a people-first organisation with a genuinely positive culture. This is a great opportunity for someone early in their finance career who wants variety, progression and to be part of a team that genuinely invests in its people.

Overview of the Accounts Assistant role:

Joining a growing finance team, the Accounts Assistant will report directly to the Senior Accountant and support the day-to-day running of the finance function. The business works with a broad range of clients, including some major names, and the finance team plays a key role in supporting the fee earners and surveyors across the business. You'll need to be confident on the phone, comfortable dealing with professional stakeholders, and have a good eye for detail. The role is primarily Manchester City Centre based, with flexible working available.

Key responsibilities of the Accounts Assistant will include:
- Processing purchase invoices, managing supplier payments and maintaining the purchase ledger
- Credit control - chasing outstanding invoices and maintaining accurate debtor records
- Bank reconciliations and daily cash management
- Supporting the preparation of month-end accounts and financial reporting
- Assisting with payroll processing and employee expense management
- Maintaining accurate financial records and supporting audit preparation
- Identifying and supporting improvements to financial processes and systems
- Providing general finance administrative support to the wider team

What we are looking for in the Accounts Assistant:
- At least 6 months' experience in an accounts or administrative role
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel
- Experience using accounting software such as Sage would be an advantage
- Organised, accurate and able to manage multiple tasks to deadlines
- Strong communicator who can work well within a collaborative team environment
- A genuine interest in developing a career in finance
- AAT studier or open to undertaking qualifications

What is on offer alongside the Accounts Assistant position:
- £28,000 - £29,000 base salary depending on experience
- Quarterly performance - shared bonus scheme based on percentage of total income
- Unlimited holiday, genuinely one of the best benefits at this level
- Flexible working - informal hybrid arrangement with 1 day per week from home
- Pension - 3% employer contribution via salary sacrifice
- Laptop and mobile phone provided
- Bar at the office and rooftop terrace, a culture that takes the social side seriously
- AAT study support available
- Access to staff discount and savings platform

How to apply for the Accounts Assistant position:

If this sounds like the right next step for you, apply today. Alternatively, contact Martin Richardson at Sellick Partnership for a confidential conversation about the role.

Sellick Partnership is proud to be an inclusive and accessible recruitment business and we support applications from candidates of all backgrounds and circumstances. Please note, our advertisements use years' experience, hourly rates, and salary levels purely as a guide and we assess applications based on the experience and skills evidenced on the CV. For information on how your personal details may be used by Sellick Partnership, please review our data processing notice on our website.

title: Asset Servicing Administrator (12 Month Fixed-Term Contract)
description:
Job Description

We are recruiting an Asset Servicing Administrator to join our Corporate Actions Processing team. You'll be responsible for the accurate and timely processing of corporate action events across multiple markets and instruments, working alongside a team of administrators to deliver an excellent service to our customers.

Asset Servicing sits within our Custody function and is made up of three teams: Event Capture, Dividends Processing and Corporate Actions Processing. We're looking for a detail-oriented individual with strong analytical skills to ensure all corporate action events are processed accurately. In this role you'll manage your own workload throughout the day, work closely with colleagues to make sure the team's work is completed, and play a key part in safeguarding client assets and minimising operational risk within a regulated environment

What does the job involve?
- Monitor, capture and process mandatory and voluntary corporate action events
- Interpret and validate information received from custodians, vendors and market announcements
- Ensure entitlements are accurately reflected in client accounts and systems
- Instructing counterparties / custodians
- Reconciling positions at different stages through the event
- Investigate and resolve reconciliation breaks promptly, escalating unresolved items to management
- Processing events to customer accounts
- Notifying customers when events are completed
- Liaise with custodians, brokers and internal teams to resolve discrepancies
- Ensuring that we are adhering with all compliance policies including AML, CASS, and breach reporting

What you'll have:
- Knowledge of the corporate action lifecycle, from announcement to settlement
- Good knowledge of financial instruments, including equities, bonds and funds
- Ability to work in high pressure deadline driven environments
- Excellent attention to detail and a risk-aware mindset
- Strong problem-solving and analytical skills
- A highly organised and methodical approach to work
- Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain complex issues clearly
- The ability to work independently and under pressure to meet tight deadlines
- A collaborative team player who is willing to share knowledge
- Advanced excel skills

About AJ Bell

At AJ Bell, we believe investing should feel good. Whether you're looking for an ISA, pension or dealing account, whether you want to invest with the help of a financial adviser or do it yourself, we have easy-to-use solutions to suit people from all walks of life.

We're one of the UK's fastest-growing investment platform businesses, trusted by everyone from professional financial advisers to first-time investors.

Today, over 762,000 customers trust us to manage more than £121.5 billion of assets. By continually striving to make investing simpler and more accessible, we're helping more people take control of their financial futures.

We're proud to be recognised as one of the UK's Best 100 Companies to Work For for six consecutive years, and a Great Place to Work in 2025 and 2026, a reflection of our supportive and collaborative culture.

What we offer the successful Customer Service Administrator
- Starting salary of £26,000 (can be higher dependent on financial services experience)
- 25 days holiday, increasing with service + buy/sell scheme + bank holidays
- 6% Pension with matched contributions
- Discretionary bonus scheme
- Share schemes (including free shares and BAYE)
- Health Cash Plan and discounted private healthcare
- Free onsite gym
- Enhanced family leave (subject to qualifying criteria)
- Travel and bike loan schemes
- Employee Assistance Programme

Life at AJ Bell
- Regular social events including summer and Christmas parties
- Learning and development opportunities tailored to you
- Casual dress code
- Friendly, supportive team environment

Our ways of working

At AJ Bell, our people are the heart of our culture. We believe in building strong connections by working together. That's why we offer a hybrid working model for our Customer Services Administrator roles, where you'll spend 3-4 days per week in the office. For new team members, the first 3 months will be spent full-time in the office to help you immerse yourself in our business and build valuable relationships with your colleagues.

Inclusion & diversity

We're committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone feels respected, supported and able to be themselves at work.

We welcome Administrator applications from all backgrounds and make hiring decisions based on skills, experience and potential.

title: Assistant Company Secretary
description:
Job Description

Good governance might happen behind the scenes, but it plays an important part in helping a business run well, make good decisions and earn the trust of its customers.

At AJ Bell, our purpose is to help people feel good investing. To deliver that, we need strong governance, clear accountability and people who are confident working at the heart of a listed business.

We're looking for an Assistant Company Secretary to join our expanding Company Secretarial team and help support the effective running of our Board, Executive Committee and their sub-committees.

This is a great opportunity to join a developing function where you'll have plenty of exposure across the business and the chance to make a real contribution. You'll work closely with senior leaders while also getting involved in the detail that keeps our governance framework running smoothly.

What does the job involve?

Reporting to the General Counsel & Company Secretary, you'll support the day-to-day operation of the Company Secretarial function. Your responsibilities will include:
- Preparing agendas, Board and committee packs, management information and meeting materials.
- Attending Board and committee meetings and producing accurate, high-quality minutes.
- Coordinating meeting schedules, annual agendas, action logs and follow-up activity.
- Supporting our governance and regulatory obligations, including requirements under company law, the Listing Rules and Market Abuse Regulation (MAR).
- Contributing to governance sections of the Annual Report and supporting preparation for the AGM.
- Maintaining statutory registers and ensuring accurate and timely Companies House filings.
- Supporting the induction and ongoing training of Board and Executive Committee members.
- Helping maintain internal governance policies, our share dealing code and insider lists.
- Supporting Board and committee effectiveness reviews and helping ensure actions are followed through.

You'll also work closely with colleagues across the business, including HR, Compliance and Finance, and support wider projects such as incentive schemes and the Senior Managers & Certification Regime (SM&CR).

What are we looking for?

You'll already have experience within company secretarial, corporate governance or a closely related environment and be comfortable working with senior stakeholders and confidential information.

We'd particularly like to hear from you if you have:
- Experience working in a company secretarial or corporate governance role, ideally gained over four or more years.
- Part or full CGI/ICSA qualification, although this isn't essential if you have strong relevant experience.
- Strong experience preparing agendas, Board papers and high-quality minutes.
- Confidence using electronic Board portals and coordinating Board and committee materials.
- Experience with statutory filings, registers and entity management.
- A good understanding of company law, governance requirements and best practice.
- Excellent organisation and attention to detail, with the ability to manage competing deadlines.
- Strong communication skills and the confidence to build relationships with stakeholders at all levels.

Experience within a listed company or financial services environment would be useful, but we're interested in the overall experience and perspective you can bring.

Most importantly, you'll be someone who takes ownership, uses good judgement and wants to contribute to a collaborative and evolving function.

About AJ Bell

At AJ Bell, we believe investing should feel good. Whether you're looking for an ISA, pension or dealing account, whether you want to invest with the help of a financial adviser or do it yourself, we have easy-to-use solutions to suit people from all walks of life.

We're one of the UK's fastest-growing investment platform businesses, trusted by everyone from professional financial advisers to first-time investors.

Today, over 762,000 customers trust us to manage more than £121.5 billion of assets. By continually striving to make investing simpler and more accessible, we're helping more people take control of their financial futures.

We're proud to be recognised as one of the UK's Best 100 Companies to Work For for six consecutive years, and a Great Place to Work in 2025 and 2026, a reflection of our supportive and collaborative culture.

What we offer
- Salary from £55,000
- 25 days holiday, increasing with service + buy/sell scheme + bank holidays
- 6% Pension with matched contributions
- Discretionary bonus scheme
- Share schemes (including free shares and BAYE)
- Health Cash Plan and discounted private healthcare
- Free onsite gym
- Enhanced family leave (subject to qualifying criteria)
- Travel and bike loan schemes
- Employee Assistance Programme

Life at AJ Bell
- Regular social events including summer and Christmas parties
- Learning and development opportunities tailored to you
- Casual dress code
- Friendly, supportive team environment

Our ways of working

We offer hybrid working, with a minimum of 50% of your working time per month spent in the office.

For new starters, there's an initial period of full-time office working to help you settle in and build relationships.

Inclusion & diversity

We're committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone feels respected and able to be themselves at work.

We welcome applications from all backgrounds and make hiring decisions based on skills, experience and potential.

title: Medical Receptionist / Administrator

This is a varied and demanding role where you will be the first point of contact for our patients. You will need to be confident, calm and compassionate, with the ability to communicate effectively with patients who may sometimes be upset, frustrated or challenging. The successful candidate will understand that GP reception is a busy and sometimes challenging environment . You will need to be able to remain calm when the phones are ringing, the waiting room is busy and patients are frustrated, while continuing to provide a professional and compassionate service. You will also need to be comfortable maintaining boundaries and following practice policies, even when dealing with difficult conversations. Previous experience within general practice and knowledge of EMIS would be highly desirable. Please do not apply if you are unable to commit to these days and hours. The role Your responsibilities will include: Welcoming patients and visitors and providing a professional and friendly first point of contact Answering a busy telephone line and dealing with patient enquiries Booking, cancelling and rearranging appointments Using EMIS to access and update patient records and manage appointments Processing prescription requests and other administrative enquiries Dealing appropriately and sensitively with confidential and sometimes complex information Liaising with GPs, nurses, pharmacists and the wider practice team Maintain accurate patient records Follow practice procedures relating to confidentiality, safeguarding and information governance Dealing professionally with difficult or challenging patients and situations Supporting colleagues and contributing to the smooth running of the practice We are a friendly practice with a 4088 patients list size. To provide a professional, efficient and welcoming reception service to patients and visitors, ensuring that patients receive appropriate assistance and are directed to the most suitable healthcare professional or service. The post holder will work as part of the wider practice team and will contribute to the effective day-to-day running of the reception and administrative functions of the practice. The role requires excellent communication skills, a calm and professional approach and the ability to deal sensitively and appropriately with patients who may be distressed, frustrated or challenging. Provide a friendly, professional and welcoming service to all patients and visitors. Act as the first point of contact for patients contacting the practice by telephone, face-to-face or through other communication channels. Answer telephone calls promptly and professionally, dealing with enquiries appropriately. Book, cancel and rearrange appointments using EMIS Web . Ensure patients are directed to the most appropriate clinician, service or healthcare provider in accordance with practice procedures. Provide patients with appropriate information regarding appointments, services and practice procedures. Deal appropriately with urgent requests and escalate concerns to the appropriate member of the clinical or management team. Assist patients who may have additional needs, including those who are elderly, vulnerable or require additional support. Accurately access and update patient records using EMIS Web. Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient information in accordance with practice procedures. Process prescription requests in line with practice policy. Process incoming and outgoing correspondence as required. Undertake administrative tasks associated with patient care and the smooth running of the practice. Complete tasks accurately and within required timescales. Maintain a good working knowledge of practice systems and procedures. Communicate clearly, professionally and courteously with patients, relatives, carers and colleagues. Remain calm and professional when dealing with difficult, distressed or angry patients. Escalate aggressive, threatening or inappropriate behaviour in accordance with practice procedures. Report any concerns regarding patient safety, safeguarding or behaviour to the appropriate member of staff. Work collaboratively with GPs, nurses, pharmacists, healthcare professionals, administrative staff and management. Support colleagues during busy periods and assist with maintaining an effective reception service. Attend team meetings and training sessions as required. Communicate relevant information effectively to colleagues. Be flexible and willing to undertake additional duties within the scope of the role when required. Maintain strict patient confidentiality at all times. Comply with GDPR, UK data protection legislation and practice information governance policies. Complete mandatory safeguarding training as required. Comply with practice health and safety policies. Report accidents, incidents, hazards and concerns appropriately.
